explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer
The Chairperson of the Law Commission of India is not the ex-officio member of the National Human Rights Commission.

Ex-officio members of NHRC:

  • Chairperson, National Commission for Scheduled Castes
  • Chairperson, National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
  • Chairperson, National Commission for Minorities
  • Chairperson, National Commission for Women
  • Chairperson, National Commission for Backward Classes
  • Chairperson National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
  • Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities

Important Tips

The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019

  • NHRC Composition: The Act allowed a former Chief Justice or Judge of the Supreme Court to become NHRC’s chairperson. The number of members increased from two to three, with at least one member being a woman. Chairpersons of commissions for Backward Classes, Child Rights, and Disabilities would also join NHRC as members.
  • SHRC Chairperson: The Bill allowed a former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court to become the chairperson of SHRC.
  • Term of Office: The term of office for NHRC and SHRC chairpersons and members was reduced to three years or until seventy years of age. The limit on reappointment for members was removed.
  • Powers of Secretary-General: The Secretary-General and Secretary of NHRC and SHRCs received broader administrative and financial powers, excluding judicial functions, under the respective chairperson’s control.
  • Union Territories: The central government could assign human rights functions of Union Territories to SHRCs, while Delhi's human rights functions would remain under NHRC’s jurisdiction.

Exp) Option b is the correct answer

question: 1. If ‘One Nation One Election’ is to be realized in India, which Article of the Indian Constitution will require an amendment?
explanation:
(Omitted) Option E: None of the above/More than one of the above
Exp) Option e is the correct answer.
The Constitution of India does not provide for simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and the state legislative assemblies. Therefore, if ‘One Nation One Election’ is to be realized in India, then Articles 83, 172, 356, and 246 would require an amendment.

Important Tips

Article 83: This Article specifies the term of the Lok Sabha. The term of the Lok Sabha is currently five years. If ‘One Nation One Election’ is to be realized, then the term of the Lok Sabha may have to be changed.
Article 172: This Article specifies the term of the state legislative assemblies. The term of the state legislative assemblies is currently five years. If ‘One Nation One Election’ is to be realized, then the term of the state legislative assemblies may have to be changed.
Article 356: This Article empowers the President of India to declare President’s Rule in a state. If ‘One Nation One Election’ is to be realized, then the provisions of Article 356 may have to be amended to ensure that President's Rule cannot be imposed in a state during the period leading up to or during the simultaneous elections.
Article 246: This Article specifies the legislative powers of the Union and the states. If ‘One Nation One Election’ is to be realized, then the provisions of Article 246 may have to be amended to ensure that the Union and the states have concurrent powers to legislate on matters relating to elections.

The Gandhi Peace Prize was instituted in 1995 by the Government to mark the 125th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. The Gandhi Peace Prize is awarded for social, economic and political transformation through non-violence, to any deserving person/s or institution/s. The award comprises a citation and an amount of Rs 1 crore. It is open to all persons regardless of nationality, race, language, caste, creed or gender and any association, institution or organisation.
Options II, III and IV are correct. The awardee is selected by a five-member jury composed of the Prime Minster of india, Chief Justice of India, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and two eminent personalities. The Prime Minister heads the jury for the prize. The decision of the jury is final and cannot be challenged or appealed.
Nominees must be proposed either by former jury members, former awardees, members of Parliament, Nobel laureates for the last five years, Secretary-General of the United Nations or heads of other international peace organisations, Vice Chancellors of universities, Chief Ministers, or Governors. Work achieved within the ten years preceding the nomination is considered for the award.
Option I is incorrect. The President of India is not a member of the jury.

Important Tips

  • Gita Press, Gorakhpur, awarded Gandhi Peace Prize for 2021.
  • Previous recipients include eminent personalities such as Nelson Mandela (2000), Coretta Scott King (2004), Qaboos bin Said Al Said (2019) and Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (2020). On 13 April 2029, the asteroid 99942 Apophis will pass safely at a distance of about 32,000 kilometers above Earth’s surface, within the geostationary orbit, posing no threat to the planet. Thus, two motions were introduced together i.e. motions regarding the Constitution (Thirteenth Amendment) Bill, 1962, and the State of Nagaland Bill, 1962. 13th Constitutional amendment Act was introduced to amend Article 371 and insertion of Artice 371 A. While State of Nagaland bill passage led to the formation of state of Nagaland.
Pair III is correct: Based on the four-fold classification of the states and territories of the Indian Union in Indian Constitution in 1950, Tripura was categorised as Part C state, and later became the Union territory based on State Reorganisation Act of 1956 and finally became the 20th state of India in 1972.

question:
1. Consider the following statements:
  2. °Right to the city” is an agreed human right and the UN-Habitat monitors the Commitments made by each country in this regard.
  3. “Right to the City” gives every occupant of the city the right to reclaim public spaces and public participation in the city.
  4. “Right to the City” means that the State cannot deny any public service or facility to the unauthorized coloniesin the city.
    Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Solution: (d)
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.
The “right to the city” is individual and collective right of all residents of a city/town/village to an equal share of its benefits and to participate in its development. It is not to be viewed as a new legalistic right, but merely as an articulation to consolidate the demand for the realisation of multiple human rights. It developed as a movement for demand of basic rights to city dwellers by Global NGO’s.
Statement 1 is Incorrect : Right to the city has developed as a response of social groups and civil society organizations to ensure better access to and opportunities for everyone living in cities, especially the most marginalized and deprived sections. Social movements and organizations from across the world worked together to develop a World Charter on the Right to the City that is also supported by UNESCO and UN Habitat, among other agencies. Hence UN HABITAT only supports and doesnot monitor the commitments made by each country in this regard.
Statements 2 and 3 are correct : The Right to city demand is based on basic human rights principles of- non discrimination; indivisibility of human rights; gender equality; progressive realisation; non-retrogression, subsidiarity; solidarity; and, cooperation. It emphasises priority attention to persons and groups in situations of vulnerability, including the homeless/landless, children, persons with disabilities, religious and sexual minorities, older persons, informal sector workers, Dalits/members of Scheduled Castes, indigenous and tribal peoples, persons from economically weaker sections, single women, and women-headed households, among others. It also stresses responsibility and sustainability as core principles.
The concept of the right to the city is a means to combat the exclusionary development, selective benefit sharing, marginalisation, and discrimination rampant in cities today.

explanation:
Solution: (d)
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.

Article 18(1) abolishes all titles. It prohibits the State to confer titles on anybody whether a citizen or a non-citizen. Military and academic distinctions are, however, exempted from the prohibition. Thus, a university can give title or honor on a man of merit.
Statement 2 is incorrect. Padma Awards were instituted in 1954 to be awarded to citizens of India in recognition of their distinguished contribution in various spheres of activity.
The government suspended the practice of granting the Padma awards for two years in 1977. It was again suspended during mid-1992 when 2 PILs were filed in the High Courts of India
They are given in three categories: Padma Vibhushan (for exceptional and distinguished service), Padma Bhushan (distinguished service of higher-order) and Padma Shri (distinguished service).
Statement 3 is incorrect. A maximum of 3 people can be awarded the Bharat Ratna.
The total number of Padma awards to be conferred each year is limited to 120. But the count excludes posthumous awards and any non-resident Indian or Overseas Citizen of India or foreign-based winners.

options: Mutual respect for each other’s territorial integrity and sovereignty
Mutual non-interference in each other’s internal affairs
explanation:
Solution: (a)

It includes principles of mutual respect for territorial integrity, non-aggression, non-interference in internal affairs, equality & mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. Important Tips

  • The five principles were subsequently modified in a form of a statement of ten principles issued in April 1955 at the historic Asian-African Conference in Bandung, Indonesia.
  • The conference itself would lead to the foundation of the Non-Aligned Movement which gave shape to the idea that the post-colonial nations had something to offer to the bipolar world of the Cold War.

Important Tips

  • The awardees are not allowed to use Bharat Ratna as a prefix or suffix to their names, as stated in Article 18(1) of the Indian Constitution.
  • There is no formal requirement that the Bharat Ratna be granted solely to Indian nationals. This prestigious prize was given to a naturalized Indian citizen, Agnes Gonxha Bojaxhiu, popularly known as Mother Teresa (1980), as well as non-Indians, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1987) and Nelson Mandela (1990).

question: 1. Which one of the following statements about ‘personal liberty’ is not correct?
options: State does not have the authority to deprive any person within the Territory of India of his/her personal liberty without any rational basis.
Basis of depriving a person of his/her personal liberty must be in accordance with procedures established by law.
Personal liberty can be secured by the judicial writ of Habeas Corpus.
The majority view of the Supreme Court in A.K. Gopalan v/s. State of Madras case invented ‘due process of law’.
explanation:
Solution: (d)
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.
“Due process of law” was already a part of the Indian legal system, inherited from the British common law tradition. The majority view in the A.K. Gopalan case held that the right to “due process of law” was not a fundamental right under the Constitution of India, allowing the state to deprive a person of their personal liberty without following established legal procedures, as long as the deprivation was not arbitrary or mala fide. However, the minority view in the same case argued that “due process of law” was indeed a fundamental right, necessitating adherence to established legal procedures even if the deprivation was not arbitrary or mala fide. Subsequently, the Supreme Court overruled its decision in the A.K. Gopalan case in the Maneka Gandhi case, holding that the right to “due process of law” is indeed a fundamental right. Consequently, the state can only deprive a person of their personal liberty if it adheres to the procedures established by law.

Important Tips

In his 1989 book Democracy and Its Critics, Dahl gives the following characteristics of a polyarchy:

  • Control over governmental decisions about policy is constitutionally vested in elected officials.

  • Practically all adults have the right to vote in these elections.
  • Most adults also have the right to run for the public offices for which candidates run in these elections.
  • Citizens have an effectively enforced right to freedom of expression, particularly political expression, including criticism of the officials, the conduct of the government, the prevailing political, economic, and social system, and the dominant ideology.

john Austin is widely credited with developing the theory of Legal Positivism. According to Legal Positivism, the law derives its authority from the recognition and acceptance by the legal system rather than from any inherent moral or natural principles.

Important Tips

Here are few features of legal positivism as explained by John Austin:

  • Separation of Law and Morality: According to legal positivism, the existence and validity of a law are not dependent on its moral or ethical qualities.
  • Command Theory of Law: Austin’s legal positivism is based on the command theory of law, which suggests that laws are essentially commands issued by a sovereign to its subjects.
  • Legal Positivism and Legal Certainty: By separating law from morality, he aimed to create a clear and concise legal system based on explicit rules and commands, enabling individuals to know their legal obligations.
  • Criticism of Natural Law: He criticized natural law concepts for being vague, subjective, and susceptible to varying interpretations. In contrast, legal positivism sought to provide a more concrete and objective foundation for the understanding and application of law.

question: 1. Who among the following said that Democracy means a system of ‘Government by Consent’?
explanation:
Solution: (a)
Exp) Option a is the correct answer
According to John Locke, democracy is a system of government by consent because the authority of the government is derived from the consent of the people it governs. He believed that individuals enter into a social contract with the government, willingly giving up some of their freedoms in exchange for the protection of their rights and the common good.

Important Tips

  • Views of J.S Mill on Democracy: Mill believed in the importance of democracy as a means to protect individual liberties and promote social progress. He argued that democracy serves as a safeguard against the potential tyranny of the majority by providing mechanisms for the protection of individual rights and freedoms.
  • Views of Jeremy Bentham on Democracy: He saw democracy as a means to achieve the greatest happiness for the greatest number of people and promote the public interest. Bentham favored representative democracy, where elected representatives make decisions on behalf of the people.
  • Views of J.J Rousseau on Democracy: According to him, a true democracy operates when the general will guides decision-making processes. Rousseau favored direct democracy, where citizens actively participate in decision-making rather than relying on elected representatives.

explanation:
Statement 1 is correct- A brand serves as a distinct symbol, logo, or name that companies utilize to differentiate their product from others in the market. Brand equity is classified as an intangible asset since its worth does not derive from a physical entity and is primarily influenced by how consumers perceive the brand.

Statement 2 is incorrect- Inventory refers to the goods or products that a company holds for sale. It represents tangible assets, as inventory consists of physical items that can be seen, touched, and measured. Therefore, it is not considered an intangible investment.

Statement 3 is correct- Intellectual property (IP) includes intangible assets such as patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets. These are legal rights that protect creations of the mind, such as inventions, artistic works, and business names. Intellectual property is considered an intangible investment as it involves the acquisition and protection of intangible assets.

Statement 4 is correct- The mailing list of clients is among the intangible assets of a company, encompassing a compilation of past customers. Building a customer list is a time-consuming process that holds substantial value for a business in the long run. It serves as an invaluable asset for targeted marketing efforts, enabling the company to promote new or existing products and services to specific customer segments. Additionally, the customer list plays a crucial role in attracting new business opportunities.

subject: Economics
question: 1. The money multiplier in an economy increases with which one of the following? [UPSC CSE Pre. 2021]
options: Increase in the Cash Reserve Ratio in the banks
Increase in the Statutory Liquidity Ratio in the banks
Increase in the banking habit of the people
Increase in the population of the country
explanation:
Money Supply is equal to Money Multiplier (m) times the amount of high powered money or the reserve money.
The money created by the RBI is the monetary base, also known as high-powered money.
The monetary base is called high-powered because the magnitude of changes in monetary base are greatly magnified by the money multiplier.
As an example, a 1% increase in monetary base may lead to a 10% increase in the money supply due to money multiplier effects.
For example, from Rs.100 can be multiplied by 5 to generate Rs.500 money supply if Reserve Ratio is 1/5 (20%) or when Money Multiplier is 5. When Reserve Ratio is 1/4 (25%) or when Money Multiplier is 4, that would generate only Rs. 400 as money supply.
The multiplier effect is an economic term, referring to the proportional amount of increase, or decrease, in final income that results from an injection, or withdrawal, of capital in effect. It measures the impact that a change in economic activity—like investment or spending—will have on the total economic output of something.
Increase in Banking habits of the people can lead to increase in money multiplier in an economy. When a customer makes a deposit into a short-term deposit account, the banking institution can lend one minus the reserve requirement to someone else. While the original depositor maintains ownership of their initial deposit, the funds created through lending are generated based on those funds. If a second borrower subsequently deposits funds received from the lending institution, this raises the value of the money supply even though no additional physical currency actually exists to support the new amount.

Important Tips

  • Rejection of Fifth Five-Year Plan: The Janata Party government rejected the existing Fifth Five-Year Plan and introduced the Rolling Plan as a more flexible alternative.
  • Three Kinds of Plans: The Rolling Plan comprised three types of plans - First Plan for the current year (annual budget), Second Plan for a fixed number of years (3, 4, or 5 years) that changed as per economic requirements, and Third Plan for long term (10, 15, or 20 years).
  • Flexibility: The Rolling Plan's advantage was its flexibility, enabling adjustments of targets, projections, and allocations to match changing economic conditions.
  • Complexity: The plan's frequent revisions led to complexity, making implementation and adherence to targets more challenging during the five-year period.

The term ‘High rate of growth of the population’ reflects that economic growth shall be less than population growth rate. There would be a lack of efficient resource mobilization. Such countries are generally low-income nations. In the below formula, more would be the denominator, less would be the per capita income.
[Per Capita Income = GDP/Population]

Option 3 is incorrect: Generally, the higher the capital formation of an economy, the faster an economy can grow its aggregate income. Producing more goods and services can lead to an increase (not decrease) in per capita income.

Option 4 is incorrect: An increase in the fiscal deficit, in theory, can boost a sluggish economy by giving more money to people who can then buy and invest more. Hence, it may increase per capita income. On the other hand, If higher fiscal deficit is due to high revenue deficit without increasing in government expenditure, then it may reduce real per capita income. So, the effect of fiscal deficit on per capita income cannot be ascertained. It depends on the reasons behind the high fiscal deficit.

1. An underdeveloped economy is generally characterized by:
  2. Low per capita income
  3. Low rate of capital formation
  4. Low dependency ratio
  5. Work force largely in the tertiary sector

Select the correct answer from the codes given below: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2017]
explanation:
An underdeveloped economy is characterized by low per capita income, low rate of capital formation, and high dependency ratio. The workforce in an underdeveloped economy is largely concentrated in the primary sector, which is the agricultural sector. The tertiary sector, which is the service sector, is not as developed in underdeveloped economies.

Important Tips

  • Low per capita income: The per capita income in an underdeveloped economy is low. Per capita income (PCI) or total income per capita is a metric used to determine the average income earned by each individual. This calculation involves dividing the total income of the area by its total population to arrive at the per capita income figure.
  • Low rate of capital formation: The rate of capital formation in an underdeveloped economy is low, which means that the country is not investing enough in its future. Capital formation refers to the net increase in a country’s stock of capital goods, which includes assets like machinery, tools, transportation equipment, and infrastructure, over a specific accounting period. A higher level of capital formation in an economy typically enables faster growth of its overall income or aggregate income.
  • High dependency ratio: The dependency ratio in an underdeveloped economy is high, which means that there are a large number of people who are not working and who are dependent on the working population for their support.
  • Workforce largely in the primary sector: The workforce in an underdeveloped economy is largely concentrated in the primary sector, which is the agricultural sector. This means that the country is not as industrialized as developed countries.

question: 1. Mixed economy in India means: [U.P.P. C.S. (Mains) 2013]

A mixed economy is an economic system that combines elements of both capitalism and socialism. In a mixed economy, the government and the private sector both play important roles in determining the direction and pace of economic development. The public sector coexists with the private sector, although they may compete for limited resources. While mixed economic systems allow the private sector to pursue profits, they also impose regulations on businesses and may nationalize industries that provide public goods.

Important Tips

Different types of economies along with their examples:

  • Capitalist Economy: A capitalist economy is characterized by private ownership of the means of production and individual freedom to engage in economic activities. The production and distribution of goods and services are primarily driven by market forces and profit motives. In this system, the government's role is minimal, and the economy operates with limited intervention. Example: The United States is often considered a prime example of a capitalist economy.
  • Mixed Economy: A mixed economy combines elements of both capitalism and socialism. In this system, there is a coexistence of private enterprises and government intervention. The government plays a significant role in certain strategic sectors and essential services while leaving other industries to the private sector. Example: India is an illustration of a mixed economy.
  • Communist Economy: A communist economy is based on the principles of social ownership of the means of production, where all means of production and distribution are owned and controlled by the state. In this system, there is no private ownership, and economic decisions are made collectively for the benefit of the entire society. The goal is to achieve a classless society with equitable distribution of resources. Example: North Korea is often cited as an example of a communist economy.
  • Socialist Economy: A socialist economy is similar to a communist economy but allows for some degree of private ownership and market mechanisms. The state still plays a significant role in the economy, but private enterprises and market forces may also operate within certain limits. Example: Sweden is an example of a socialist economy.

explanation:
The First Five Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on developing agriculture, aiming for self-sufficiency in food production and increased productivity. It emphasized land reforms, modernization, and improved irrigation facilities. The plan aimed to establish the groundwork for sustained economic growth and overall development of India, as agriculture was a vital sector of the economy at that time.

Important Tips

Key Highlights of First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956):

  • Focus on Primary Sector: The plan prioritized the development of the primary sector, especially agriculture, to achieve self-sufficiency in food production.
  • Harrod-Domar Model: Based on the Harrod-Domar model, the plan aimed to promote capital formation and investment to boost economic growth.
  • Allocation of Planned Budget: The planned budget of ₹2,069 crore was allocated to seven broad areas, including irrigation, energy, agriculture, industry, and social services.
  • Active Role of State: The plan emphasized an active role of the state in all economic sectors due to low capital availability and saving capacity after independence.
  • Growth Achievements: The targeted growth rate was 2.1% GDP growth, but the achieved growth rate was 3.6%, with a 15% increase in net domestic product and 8% rise in per capita income.
  • Infrastructure Development: Several irrigation projects like Bhakra, Hirakund, and Damodar Valley dams were initiated, and five Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) were established.

  • If annual wages increase equal to increase in inflation rate during same period, there would be no change in real wage or real income.
  • If annual wages increase more than increase in inflation rate during same period, there would be increase in real wage or real income.
  • If inflation rate increases more than increase in annual wages during same period, there would be decrease in real wage or real income.

explanation:
NITI Aayog, established in January 2015, replaced the Planning Commission. Based on Cooperative Federalism, NITI Aayog fosters collaboration between the central and state governments for addressing diverse issues. NITI Aayog does not have a full-time Chairman. The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio Chairman of NITI Aayog. The Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog is the head of the organization and is responsible for its day-to-day operations.

Important Tips

Members of NITI Aayog
The NITI Aayog comprises the following:

  • A Governing Council composed of Chief Ministers of all the States and Union territories with Legislatures and lieutenant governors of Union Territories (except Delhi and Puducherry).
  • Regional Councils composed of Chief Ministers of States and Lt. Governors of Union Territories in the region to address specific issues and contingencies impacting more than one state or a region.
  • Full-time organizational framework composed of
    • a Vice-Chairperson,
    • four full-time members,
    • two part-time members (from leading universities, research organizations and other relevant institutions in an ex-officio capacity),
    • four ex-officio members of the Union Council of Ministers,
    • a Chief Executive Officer (with the rank of Secretary to the Government of India) who looks after administration, and a secretariat.
  • Experts and specialists in various fields.

subject: Economics
question: 1. Which one of the following is a sign of economic growth? [R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 2013]
options: An increase in National Income at constant prices during a year.
A sustained increase in real Per Capita Income.
An increase in National Income at current prices over time.
An increase in National Income along with an increase in population.
explanation:
Real per capita income is a measure of a country’s economic well-being that takes into account the purchasing power of its citizens. It is calculated by dividing the country’s gross domestic product (GDP) by its population, and then adjusting for inflation. It is considered the best sign of economic growth in a real sense. For instance, India is the world’s 5th largest economy but on a per capita income basis, India ranked 141st by GDP (nominal). Hence, increase in GDP, NNP, NDP over time do not reflect the real picture of economic growth. Even nations are divided into developed, developing or poor based on per capita income. So, an increase in real per capita income is the best sign of economic growth.

Important Tips

For Example: To arrive at the change in real income of farmers, we need to adjust the current income of the farmers with an appropriate inflation index. If the inflation in the economy is higher than the farm produce prices then actually it reduces the real income of farmers. And when prices received by farmers for agricultural produce rise faster than the inflation, it adds to the real income, even without an increase in the volume of output.

question: 1. Which of the following is not a method to calculate the Gross Domestic Product (GDP)? [66th B.P.S.C. (Pre) (Re-Exam) 2020]
explanation:
The total final value of goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country in a specified time period (generally a financial year) is called Gross Domestic Product. GDP can be calculated by three methods: Product method, Income method and Expenditure method. Diminishing cost method is not a way to calculate GDP.

Important Tips

  • The Product or Value-Added Method: In this method, we calculate the aggregate annual value of goods and services produced. To achieve this, we add up the value of all goods and services produced by all the firms in an economy.
  • Expenditure Method: An alternative way to calculate GDP is by looking at the expenditure side of all the sectors. Whatever goods and services are produced in the economy, they are ultimately purchased by the four sectors of the economy i.e., household sector, government sector, private sector and external sector. So, if we add the expenditures made by these four sectors on the purchase of final goods and services produced by the firms within the domestic territory then it shall be equal to the GDP of the country.
  • GDP = C + I + G + X - M [C: Household consumption; I: Investment by private sector; G: Government sector expenditure on both capital and consumption goods; X: Exports from India; M: Total imports by India]
  • Income Method: The sum of the final goods produced in the economy must be equal to the income received by all the four factors of production i.e., wages, rents, interests and profits.
  • GDP = Profit earned by all the firms + Interest received by all the capital deployed + Rent received for the natural resources + Wages earned by all the laborers
  • GDP = Profit + Interest + Rent + Wages

question:
1. Consider the following statements regarding Public Goods and Externalities:
  2. Non-rivalry and non-excludability are two characteristics of Public Goods
  3. Market can provide the optimal amount of a good in the presence of externalities

Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [CAPF 2024]
explanation:
Statement 1 is correct. Public goods are a special category of goods that are non-rivalrous and non-excludable. Non-rivalry means that one person’s use of the good does not reduce its availability to others. Non-excludability means that no one can be effectively prevented from using the good. Classic examples include National Defence, street lighting, and clean air. These features make it difficult for the private market to charge users, which often leads to underproduction or complete absence of such goods in a free market.

Statement 2 is incorrect. In the presence of externalities (both positive and negative), markets usually fail to provide the socially optimal amount of the good or service. This is because externalities lead to costs or benefits that are not reflected in market prices. For example, pollution is a negative externality where the producer does not bear the full cost, and education is a positive externality where the consumer does not capture the full benefit. In both cases, market outcomes are inefficient without government intervention.

question:
1. Consider the following statements about indifference curves.
  2. Indifference curves are convex to the origin.
  3. Higher indifference curve represents higher level of satisfaction.
  4. Two indifference curves cut each other.
    Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Statement 1 is correct- Indifference curves are convex to the origin. This means that the consumer is willing to give up less of one good in order to get more of the other good, the more of the first good they already have. For example, let's say you have Rs. 20 to spend on pizza and ice cream (assuming you like both and want maximum satisfaction from your purchase). You can buy 4 pizzas and no ice cream or 2 pizzas and 2 ice creams. You are indifferent between these two combinations because they both cost Rs. 20 and give you the same amount of satisfaction. However, you cannot buy 5 pizzas and 1 ice cream, because that would cost more than Rs. 20. If you tried to buy 5 pizzas and 1 ice cream, you would have to give up some of the pizza in order to afford the ice cream. This would make you less happy, because you would be consuming less of the goods that you prefer (pizza).
Statement 2 is correct- Higher indifference curves represent higher levels of satisfaction. This means that the consumer prefers any combination of goods on a higher indifference curve to any combination of goods on a lower indifference curve.
Statement 3 is incorrect- Indifference curves never intersect. This is because if two indifference curves intersected, it would mean that the consumer was indifferent between two different combinations of goods, which is not possible.

  • Oligopoly: Oligopoly is a market structure characterized by a small number of large firms that dominate the market. question:
1. Suppose the revenue expenditure is ₹ 80,000 crores and the revenue receipts of the Government are ₹ 60,000 crores. The Government budget also shows borrowings of ₹ 10,000 crores and interest payments of ₹ 6,000 crores. Which of the following statements are correct?
    I. Revenue deficit is ₹ 20,000 crores.
    II. Fiscal deficit is ₹ 10,000 crores.
    III. Primary deficit is ₹ 4,000 crores.
    Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.
Given Data:

  • Revenue Expenditure = ₹ 80,000 crores
  • Revenue Receipts = ₹ 60,000 crores
  • Borrowings (Fiscal Deficit) = ₹ 10,000 crores
  • Interest Payments = ₹ 6,000 crores

Statement I is correct: Revenue Deficit
Definition:
Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts
Calculation:
Revenue Expenditure = ₹ 80,000 crores
Revenue Receipts = ₹ 60,000 crores
So, Revenue Deficit = ₹ 80,000 - ₹ 60,000 = ₹ 20,000 crores

Statement II is correct: Fiscal Deficit
Definition:
Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure - Total Receipts (excluding borrowings)
In this question, total borrowings by the government are ₹ 10,000 crores, which means the gap between the government's total expenditure and its non-borrowed receipts is being met by borrowing ₹ 10,000 crores.
Fiscal Deficit is the total borrowing requirement of the government. In the given scenario, the borrowings directly represent the fiscal deficit.
Fiscal Deficit = Borrowings = 10,000 crores

Statement III is correct: Primary Deficit
Definition:
Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments
Calculation:
Fiscal Deficit = ₹ 10,000 crores
Interest Payments = ₹ 6,000 crores
Primary Deficit = ₹ 10,000 - ₹ 6,000 = ₹ 4,000 crores
Hence, All three statements are correct.

This renders an economy vulnerable if the economy is already facing economic crisis as it has an obligation to return the debt as well as interest payments (debt service). Example: Many economies like Mexico, Argentina etc who faced crisis were seen to have borrowed large amounts of short-maturity debt. So, the ideal scenarios is not to depend upon short-term debt during crisis.
Statement 2 is incorrect: Opening up to the foreign banks and depending upon them is not a good idea during crisis. It has been empirically observed in World Bank Research that in many cases (like during Global Financial Crisis 2007-08) that foreign banks reduced their lending during crisis. Many of them choose to retreat from cross-border banking in general, including through cutting back on new entry.
Statement 3 is incorrect: Capital account convertibility would mean that there is no restriction on conversion of the domestic currency into a foreign currency. It is recognised that capital flows are sensitive to macroeconomic conditions. Any deterioration in fiscal conditions, inflation management, balance of payments, or any other economic crisis may cause a cessation or reversal of capital flows. This might make the economy vulnerable if it already suffering from economic crisis.

question:
1. Consider the following items:
  2. Cereal grains hulled
  3. Chicken eggs cooked
  4. Fish processed and canned
  5. Newspapers containing advertising material
    Which of the above items is/are exempted under GST (Goods and Services Tax)?
explanation:
Exp) Option c is the correct answer.
Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct.
The Goods and Services Tax in India is comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based value-added indirect tax. It has replaced many central and state indirect taxes in India such as the excise duty, VAT, services tax, etc.
There are four slabs for taxes for both goods and services 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%. Although GST aimed at levying a uniform tax rate on all products and services, four different tax slabs were introduced because daily necessities could not be subject to the same rate as luxury items. A number of items are exempted from GST i.e. they are kept at zero or nil GST rate.
Items exempted from GST include fresh or pasteurized milk, butter milk, curd, chena or paneer, and non-vegetarian items like eggs (cooked or raw), chicken, fresh meat, and fresh or chilled fish. Fruits, vegetables, as well as unit container-packed frozen branded vegetables (uncooked or steamed) are also exempt.
Other items on this list include natural honey, hulled cereal grains (like barley, wheat, oat), Palmyra jiggery etc.
There are other items on the exempted list like manuscripts, postal items like envelope and post cards sold by the government, newspapers, journals and periodicals, whether illustrated or containing advertising material etc.
Statement 3 is incorrect: Fish, crustaceans, molluscs & other aquatic invertebrates in processed, cured or frozen state are taxable at 5% rate under GST.
The items that are kept outside the purview of GST are petroleum products (such as petroleum crude, motor spirit, diesel, aviation turbine fuel and natural gas), electricity and alcohol for human consumption.

Important Tips

  • The Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) has been constituted vide GOI notification dated 30th December, 2010.
  • The Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and its members are Governor, Reserve Bank of India; Finance Secretary and/or Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs; Secretary, Department of Financial Services; Chief Economic Adviser, Ministry of Finance; Chairman, Securities and Exchange Board of India; Chairman, Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority and Chairman, Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority.
  • The Council deals, inter-alia, with issues relating to financial stability, financial sector development, inter-regulatory coordination, financial literacy, financial inclusion and macro prudential supervision of the economy including the functioning of large financial conglomerates. No funds are separately allocated to the Council for undertaking its activities.
  • The Council and its Sub-Committee (chaired by Governor, Reserve Bank of India) deliberate on agenda items proposed by any of the members of the Council which broadly include matters relating to financial stability, inter-regulatory coordination, and financial sector development. question:
1. Which of the following action(s) by the Government would lead to contraction of money supply in the economy?
  2. Purchase of Treasury Bills by the central bank from public
  3. Sale of Treasury Bills by the central bank to public
  4. Sale of foreign exchange by the central bank
  5. Purchase of foreign exchange by the central bank
    Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation:
Exp) Option c is the correct answer
Money supply represents the total amount of cash, coins, and other liquid assets available in an economy at a particular time. The central bank plays a vital role in controlling the money supply through monetary policy such as Open Market Operation and
Option 1 is incorrect: Treasury bills are short term money market, debt instruments issued by the Government of India. The purchase of Treasury Bills by the central bank from public will increase the money supply in the market leading to expansion of money supply rather than contraction of money supply in the market.
Option 2 is correct: When the central bank sells Treasury Bills, the public pays money to purchase them, which reduces the money supply in the economy. This action leads to a contraction of the money supply.
Option 3 is correct: When the central bank sells foreign exchange, it absorbs money from the economy, reducing the domestic money supply leading to a contraction of the money supply.
Option 4 is incorrect: When the central bank buys foreign exchange, it increases the money into the economy leading to an expansion of the money supply.

Important Tips

Instruments of Monetary Policy:

  • Repo Rate: The interest rate at which the Reserve Bank provides liquidity under the liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) to all LAF participants, using government and other approved securities as collateral.
  • Reverse Repo Rate: The interest rate at which the Reserve Bank absorbs liquidity from banks against the collateral of eligible government securities under the LAF. Following the introduction of SDF, the fixed rate reverse repo operations will be at the discretion of the RBI for specified purposes.
  • Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) Rate: The rate at which the Reserve Bank accepts uncollateralised deposits on an overnight basis from all LAF participants.
  • Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) Rate: The penal rate at which banks can borrow on an overnight basis from the Reserve Bank by dipping into their Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) portfolio up to a predefined limit (2%).
  • Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR): The average daily balance that a bank is required to maintain with the Reserve Bank as a percentage of its net demand and time liabilities (NDTL), as notified by the Reserve Bank in the Official Gazette.
  • Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR): Every bank must maintain assets in India, not less than a certain percentage of its demand and time liabilities. These assets are typically in unencumbered government securities, cash, and gold, as specified by the Reserve Bank.
  • Open Market Operations (OMOs): The outright purchase/sale of government securities by the Reserve Bank to inject or absorb durable liquidity into the banking system.

subject: Economics
question:
1. Consider the following statements:
  2. Burden of a tax on a commodity is independent of who (buyer or seller) it is explicitly imposed upon.
  3. Burden of a tax on a commodity depends on the slope of the demand and supply curves.
    Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Exp) Option c is the correct answer
When a tax is imposed on a good, it increases the price paid by the buyer or reduces the price received by the seller. The final burden of this tax, called tax incidence, is shared between buyers and sellers depending on how the market responds.
Statement 1 is correct: The burden of a tax does not depend on whom the tax is legally imposed upon. Even if the government asks the seller to pay the tax, the seller may raise the price and pass some of it to the buyer. Similarly, if the tax is imposed on the buyer, they may ask the seller to reduce the price. So, the economic burden is shared based on market forces, not legal responsibility.
Statement 2 is correct: The way the tax burden is divided depends on how sensitive buyers and sellers are to price changes, which is shown by the slope of the demand and supply curves.

  • If demand is less sensitive (inelastic), buyers bear more of the tax.
  • If supply is less sensitive (inelastic), sellers bear more of the tax.
    This means the more flexible side of the market escapes more of the burden, while the less flexible side bears more.

The NIRVIK scheme, also known as the Niryat Rin Vikas Yojana, was announced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during the Union Budget 2020-21 in the Indian Parliament. The primary aim of the NIRVIK scheme is to support the export sector, boost exports, and address the challenges faced by exporters in terms of credit availability, insurance coverage, and high-interest rates.

Important Tips

Key features of the NIRVIK scheme:

  • High insurance cover: The scheme provides for a high insurance cover to protect exporters against non-payment or delayed payment for their exports.
  • Reduction in premium: Small exporters benefit from reduced premium rates under the scheme, making it more affordable for them to insure their export transactions.
  • Simplified claim settlement: The procedures for claim settlement are simplified, making it easier and quicker for exporters to receive compensation in case of loss due to non-payment.
  • Coverage of principal and interest: The NIRVIK scheme covers up to 90% of the principal and interest amount, providing a significant safety net for exporters.
  • Premium subsidy: The Ministry proposed to subsidize the premium paid by exporters belonging to certain key sectors, further reducing their financial burden.
  • Enhanced credit rating: The Export Credit Guarantee Corporation (ECGC) cover under the scheme enhances the credit rating of the borrower to an AA rating. This improvement in credit rating benefits exporters by allowing them to access credit at lower interest rates.
  • Interest rate benefits: With the enhanced credit cover, exporters can avail themselves of lower interest rates on both Foreign and Rupee export credit, with rates falling below 4% and 8% respectively.

question:
1. Which of the following are the sources of income for the Reserve Bank of India?
    I. Buying and selling Government bonds
    II. Buying and selling foreign currency
    III. Pension fund management
    IV. Lending to private companies
    V. Printing and distributing currency notes
    Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.
The Reserve Bank of India was established under the RBI Act, 1934, to regulate the issuance of banknotes and maintain monetary stability in India. While its primary goal is public welfare, certain market operations undertaken to ensure financial stability also generate income. This surplus is transferred to the Government of India as per the Bimal Jalan Committee’s (2019) recommendations on the economic capital framework.

Option I is correct: Open market operations, through which the RBI buys or sells government bonds to regulate the money supply, serve as a key source of income. In addition to earning interest on these bonds, the RBI can also gain from favorable movements in bond prices.

Option II is correct: As per Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA), the RBI is responsible for managing the country’s foreign exchange reserves and ensuring external stability. The RBI’s activities in the foreign exchange market also contribute to its profits. For example, it may purchase U.S. dollars at lower rates and sell them at higher rates later.

Option III is incorrect: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) does not manage pension funds. Pension fund management in India is regulated and overseen by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

Option IV is incorrect: The RBI does not directly lend to private companies in India. It lends money mainly to commercial banks and financial institutions who in turn lend to private companies and individuals.

Option V is correct: The RBI Act, 1934 designates the Reserve Bank of India as the sole authority to issue banknotes in India. While the RBI bears the printing costs, it earns seigniorage—the profit arising from the difference between the face value of the currency and its production cost which also acts as one of the sources of income of RBI.

options: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement I explains Statement II

Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.
Statement I is correct: Companies raise long-term funds either by issuing bonds or by selling stocks. When a company issues bonds, it is essentially borrowing money from investors, who are known as bondholders. On the other hand, when a company issues stocks, it is selling ownership shares to investors called stockholders (or shareholders). Regarding returns from an investment in a company, generally, bondholders are considered to be relatively at lower risk than stockholders.

Statement II is correct: A stockholder is considered as the owner of the company with equity rights, while a bondholder is a creditor who lends money and holds no ownership in the company.

Statement III is correct: Bondholders are given repayment priority over stockholders because bonds are issued for a fixed term with a predetermined interest rate and are repayable at maturity. In contrast, capital from shares is not typically returned during the company’s lifetime, and returns to stockholders vary based on the company’s profits.

Thus bondholders are considered as the relatively lower risk than stockholders because bondholders are with no ownership stake, they have a legal right to fixed repayments and are prioritized over stockholders who are the owners of the company and receive returns based on the profit of the company. Hence Option a is correct: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I.

question:
1. Consider the following statements in respect of RTGS and NEFT:
    I. In RTGS, the settlement time is instantaneous while in case of NEFT, it takes some time to settle payments.
    II. In RTGS, the customer is charged for inward transactions while that is not the case for NEFT.
    III. Operating hours for RTGS are restricted on certain days while this is not true for NEFT.
    Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Exp) option a is the correct answer.
Statement I is correct:
RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement): As the name suggests, RTGS transactions are processed in “real-time” and on a “gross” basis. This means each transaction is settled individually as it is received, with virtually no waiting period. The beneficiary bank typically receives the funds in real-time, and the beneficiary’s account is credited within a short time (usually within 30 minutes of receiving the transfer message).
NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer): NEFT operates on a “Deferred Net Settlement” (DNS) basis. This means transactions are collected and processed in batches at specific intervals. While NEFT is now available 24x7, the actual settlement still happens in half-hourly batches. So, it takes some time for the payment to be settled.

Statement II is incorrect: According to RBI guidelines, inward RTGS transactions (receiving money) are free of charge. Banks are not permitted to levy any charges on the beneficiary for receiving funds via RTGS. Similarly, inward NEFT transactions are also free of charge.

Statement III is incorrect: Previously, both RTGS and NEFT operated only during specific hours on working days. However, major reforms by the Reserve Bank of India have now made both services available 24x7, 365 days a year. NEFT became a round-the-clock service in 2019, followed by RTGS in 2020. This means that customers can now transfer funds using either system at any time of the day, on any day of the year, including weekends and bank holidays.

subject: Economics
question: 1. Which one of the following activities of the Reserve Bank of India is considered to be part of ‘sterilization’?
options: Debt and cash management for the Central and State Governments
Regulating the functions of Non-banking Financial Institutions
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.
Sterilization refers to the actions taken by a central bank to offset the impact of its foreign exchange operations on the domestic money supply. When a central bank intervenes in the foreign exchange market by buying or selling foreign currencies, it affects the domestic money supply. Open Market Operations (OMO) is one of the primary tools used by central banks, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), to conduct monetary policy. In OMO, the central bank buys or sells government securities (bonds) in the open market to influence the liquidity in the economy. When the RBI conducts OMO, it impacts the money supply in the economy. If the RBI buys government securities, it injects money into the system, increasing the money supply. To prevent this injection of money from creating inflationary pressures, the RBI engages in sterilization. Sterilization involves the simultaneous sale or purchase of other securities, typically treasury bills, to offset the impact of the initial open market operation.

Important Tips

  • Oversight of settlement payment systems refers to the role of the Reserve Bank of India in supervising and ensuring the smooth functioning of payment and settlement systems in the country. Payment systems facilitate the transfer of funds between individuals, businesses, and financial institutions.
  • Debt and cash management for the Central and State Governments involves the Reserve Bank of India’s role in managing the issuance, redemption, and servicing of government debt, as well as overseeing the cash flow operations of the government. This function is important for maintaining government finances and liquidity.
  • The Reserve Bank of India regulates and supervises non-banking financial institutions (NBFIs) such as non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). NBFIs play a crucial role in the financial system by providing various financial services.

options: Borrowing from the public to finance budget deficit
Borrowing from the banks to finance a budget deficit

explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.
Deficit financing means generating funds to finance the deficit which results from excess of expenditure over revenue. The gap being covered by borrowing from the public by the sale of bonds or by printing new money.

Government expenditure by printing money boosts incomes and raises private demand in the economy. Thus, it fuels inflation. A little increase in inflation is healthy as it encourages business activity. But if the government doesn't stop in time, more and more money floods the market and creates high inflation. And since inflation is revealed with a lag, it is often too late before governments realise, they have over-borrowed. A lender of last resort is an institution, usually a country’s central bank, that offers loans to banks or other eligible institutions that are experiencing financial difficulty or are considered highly risky or near collapse. Commercial banks usually try not to borrow from the lender of last resort because such action indicates that the bank is experiencing a financial crisis.

  3. Fiscal stimulus
  4. Inflation-indexing wages
  5. Higher purchasing power
  6. Rising interest rates
    Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.
Demand-pull inflation is the upward pressure on prices that follows a shortage in supply, a condition that economists describe as “too many dollars chasing too few goods.”

Expansionary policies: When the government spends more freely, money in the market is increased. It leads to increase demand for the goods and fuels demand-pull inflation.

Fiscal Stimulus: It also increases the money in the market leads to increase demand for the goods and fuels demand-pull inflation.

Higher Purchasing Power: When consumers earn higher income, they feel confident and spend more. This leads to more demand and fuels Demand-pull inflation.

Inflation-indexing wages and rising interest rates do not increase or cause demand-pull inflation.

question:
1. If the RBI decides to adopt an expansionist monetary policy, which of the following would it not do?
  2. Cut and optimize the Statutory Liquidity Ratio
  3. Increase the Marginal Standing Facility Rate
  4. Cut the Bank Rate and Repo Rate
    Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer.
Expansionary monetary policy is when the Reserve Bank of India uses its monetary policy tools to stimulate the economy. That increases the money supply, lowers interest rates, and increases demand.

Statements 1 is incorrect. A reduction in SLR would mean higher liquidity for the banks, so they would have more funds to lend. This would tend to reduce lending rates and increase demand in the economy. The SLR is the reserve that the commercial banks in India are required to maintain in the form of cash, gold reserves, government approved securities before providing credit to the customers.

Statement 2 is correct. Marginal Standing facility (MSF) is a special window for the commercial banks to borrow from the RBI against approved government securities, in case of an emergency such as an acute cash shortage. MSF rate is generally higher than Repo rate. An increase in the MSF rate leads to higher borrowing cost for the banks and thus, reduces money supply in the economy. It is a contractionary monetary policy.

Statements 3 is incorrect. A cut in repo rate means cost of borrowing from the Reserve Bank will be lower for commercial banks. The rate cut will further help banks to lower loan interest rates for borrowers.

  2. Minimum Support Price
  3. Government's trading
  4. Government’s stockpiling
  5. Consumer subsidies
    Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.
Statement 1 and 3 are correct. Minimum Support Price (MSP) is a form of market intervention by the Government of India to insure agricultural producers against any sharp fall in farm prices. The major objectives are to support the farmers from distress sales and to procure food grains for public distribution. According to the economic survey 2019-20, prices of rice and wheat remained stable since 2014 due to adequate supply arising out of sufficient domestic production and also due to maintenance of adequate buffer stock of rice and wheat for meeting the food security requirements. As a result, the price volatility was lower in the case of rice and wheat.

Statement 2 is correct. The government typically buys more than a third of the country’s rice output at a fixed price, which has a direct impact on prices paid by traders and consumers. According to economic survey 2019-20, to ensure adequate availability of wheat and rice in central pool, to keep a check on the open market prices and to ensure food security, the Central Government has undertaken a number of measures, which include: -

  • State Governments, particularly those undertaking Decentralized Procurement (DCP), are encouraged to maximize procurement of wheat and rice.
  • Strategic reserves of 5 million tonnes of food grains over the operational stocks are maintained to be used in extreme situations.
  • Sale of wheat and rice is undertaken through Open Market Sale Scheme (OMSS) (Domestic) so as to check inflationary trend in prices of foodgrains.

Statement 4 is correct. The National Food Security Act, 2013 provides for coverage of up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population for receiving subsidized food grains. Under the act, the ration cardholders are allowed to buy 5 kg of food grains per person each month at a subsidised rate of ₹2 per kg of wheat and ₹3 per kg of rice.

1. With reference to India, consider the following:
  2. Nationalization of Banks
  3. Formation of Regional Rural Banks
  4. Adoption of villages by Bank Branches
    Which of the above can be considered as steps taken to achieve the ‘financial inclusion’ in India?
explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.
The steps taken to achieve ‘financial inclusion’ in India are:

  • Nationalization of Banks: The nationalization of banks refers to the process of transferring the ownership and control of private banks to the government. The first phase of nationalization of banks took place in 1969, when 14 major commercial banks were nationalized. The second phase took place in 1980, when six more banks were nationalized. The main objective of nationalization of banks was to extend banking facilities to rural and semi-urban areas, and to prioritize the credit needs of the neglected sectors, such as agriculture, small-scale industries, exports, etc.
  • Formation of Regional Rural Banks: The Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) are local-level banking institutions that operate in different states of India. They were established in 1975 under the RRB Act, 1976, with the aim of providing credit and other facilities to the rural areas, especially to the small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers, artisans, and small entrepreneurs. The RRBs are jointly owned by the Central Government, the State Government, and a sponsor bank (usually a public sector bank).
  • Adoption of villages by Bank Branches: The adoption of villages by bank branches is a scheme initiated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 2010, under which each bank branch in a district has to adopt at least one village (unbanked or underbanked) and provide banking services to all the households in that village. The scheme aims to ensure that every household has at least one bank account and access to other financial products and services, such as savings, remittances, insurance, pension, etc.

question: 1. Which one of the following is not an instrument of selective credit control in India?
explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.
Selective credit control is a qualitative method of credit control by the central bank that aims to regulate the distribution or direction of bank resources to particular sectors of the economy in accordance with broad national priorities.

Variable cost reserve ratios is not an instrument of selective credit control because it is a quantitative method of credit control that involves changing the percentage of deposits that banks have to keep as reserves with the central bank.

Important Tips

Some of the instruments of selective credit control are:

  • Regulation of consumer credit: This involves setting the down payment and maximum maturities of instalment credit for durable goods such as automobiles, refrigerators, etc. This helps to curb the excessive demand for consumer goods and inflationary pressures.
  • Rationing of credit: This involves fixing the maximum amount of credit that banks can lend for certain purposes or to certain sectors. This helps to divert credit from less essential to more essential activities and prevent speculative hoarding of essential commodities.
  • Margin requirements: This involves fixing the minimum margin or percentage of down payment that borrowers have to make while obtaining loans against specific securities such as stocks, bonds, gold, etc. This helps to regulate the volume and value of credit and prevent excessive speculation in the capital market.
  • Moral suasion: This involves persuading or advising the banks by the central bank to follow a certain course of action or policy in their lending operations. This helps to influence the banks’ behaviour without any legal compulsion or penalty.

question: 1. Money multiplier in India is defined as :
explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer.
Money multiplier is a term used in economics to describe the amount of money that is created by the banking system in relation to the amount of money that is deposited in the system. In India, the money multiplier is calculated as the ratio of broad money (M3) to reserve money (M0), where:

  • Broad money (M3) is the sum of currency with the public, demand deposits with banks, and time deposits with banks.
  • Reserve money (M0) is the sum of currency in circulation, bankers’ deposits with the RBI, and ‘other’ deposits with the RBI

Important Tips

  • The money multiplier indicates how much the banking system can expand the money supply by lending out a fraction of their deposits, while keeping a fraction as reserves.
  • The higher the reserve ratio, the lower the money multiplier, and vice versa.
  • The current money multiplier in India is not a fixed or static number, as it is influenced by various factors such as the reserve ratio, demand for credit, and lending practices of the banking system

options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Assertion is correct: Cost push inflation is caused by shift in aggregate supply curve. Cost push inflation is a type of inflation that occurs when supply falls drastically and demand remains at the same level. This creates excess demand in the economy, and supply cannot match it, causing prices to rise. Such situations arise due to supply-side shocks, such as increase in costs of production or decrease in availability of resources. These shocks shift the aggregate supply curve to the left, resulting in a higher price level and lower real GDP.

Reason is correct: Shift in aggregate supply curve takes place because of increase in wages. One of the possible causes of cost push inflation is the increase in wages of labour without any increase in its productivity. This increases the marginal cost of production for firms, and reduces their profits. To maintain their profit margins, firms pass on the higher costs to consumers by raising their prices. This shifts the aggregate supply curve to the left, causing cost push inflation

subject: Economics
question: 1. Which one of the following situations can lead to inflation?
options: Rapid growth of aggregate demand outweighing supply
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.
Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services in an economy over time. It occurs when the demand for goods and services surpasses the available supply, leading to upward pressure on prices.
Option a is correct: When aggregate demand (the total demand for goods and services in an economy) increases rapidly and outpaces the available supply, it creates a situation where there is excess demand in the economy. To meet this higher demand, producers may increase prices, leading to inflationary pressures.

Option b is incorrect: A sluggish growth of aggregate demand generally does not lead to inflation. In fact, it can result in deflationary pressures, where there is insufficient demand to absorb the available supply, leading to a decrease in prices.

Option c is incorrect: A reduction in the money supply can also lead to deflationary pressures rather than inflation. When the money supply decreases, it can reduce overall spending and aggregate demand, leading to a decrease in prices.

Option d is incorrect: Higher levels of unemployment are typically associated with a slowdown in economic activity and lower aggregate demand. In this scenario, there is a lack of purchasing power in the economy, which can put downward pressure on prices, leading to deflation rather than inflation.

When someone borrows money, they agree to pay back the original amount borrowed (the principal) plus an additional amount known as interest. The nominal interest rate is the rate at which this interest is calculated and expressed as a percentage of the principal.

Important Tips:

  • Bank rate, also known as the discount rate or base rate, is the rate at which central banks lend money to commercial banks. It is used as a tool by central banks to control money supply and influence interest rates in the economy.
  • Real interest rate refers to the nominal interest rate adjusted for inflation. It represents the actual purchasing power or real return of an investment or loan after accounting for inflation.
  • Terms of credit generally refer to the conditions and terms under which credit is extended, including repayment period, interest rate, collateral requirements, and other related terms.

1. Which of the following will be the outcome if an economy is under inflationary pressure?
  2. Domestic currency heads depreciation.
  3. Exports become less competitive imports become costlier.
  4. Cost of borrowing decreases
  5. Bondholders benefit.
    Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Exp) Option c is the correct answer.
Statement 1 is correct- Inflationary pressure can lead to a depreciation of the domestic currency when there is a decrease in the purchasing power, causing the value of the currency relative to other currencies to decline.

Statement 2 is incorrect- The impact of inflation on trade competitiveness varies based on factors such as exchange rates, relative price levels, and demand conditions, and it is not always a direct outcome of inflationary pressure.

Statement 3 is correct- During inflationary periods, central banks often implement expansionary monetary policies to stimulate the economy, which can involve lowering interest rates to encourage borrowing and spending, reducing the cost of loans for individuals and businesses.

Statement 4 is incorrect- Bondholders are not necessarily benefitted and creditors are not necessarily at loss in an economy with inflationary pressure. It depends on the type of bond and the terms of the loan. In general, bonds with a fixed interest rate lose value in an inflationary environment. This is because the real value of the interest payments decreases as inflation increases. However, bonds with an inflation indexation clause adjust the interest payments according to the inflation rate, so they do not lose value in an inflationary environment.

1. Consider the following statements regarding instruments of Monetary Policy:
  2. The Central Bank can increase the money supply by increasing the bank rate
  3. The Central Bank can increase the money supply by purchasing securities from the public
  4. The Central Bank can decrease the money supply by increasing the cash reserve ratio
    Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Exp) Option b is the correct answer
The Central Bank, such as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), uses various tools to control the money supply in the economy. This set of tools is collectively known as monetary policy. Its primary aim is to ensure price stability, manage inflation, and support economic growth.
Some of the key instruments of monetary policy include:

  • Bank Rate: the rate at which the Central Bank lends to commercial banks.
  • Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR): the percentage of deposits that banks must keep with the Central Bank.
  • Open Market Operations (OMO): buying or selling of government securities in the open market.
  • Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Repo/Reverse Repo Rates are also important tools.

Statement 1 is incorrect. Raising the bank rate makes borrowing costlier for banks. This discourages them from borrowing from the Central Bank, leading to a reduction in money supply and not an increase.

Statement 2 is correct. Through Open Market Operations, when the Central Bank purchases government securities from the public or banks, it releases money into the economy. This increases the money supply.

Statement 3 is correct. When the CRR is increased, banks are required to hold more of their funds with the RBI. This reduces the money they can lend, thereby decreasing the money supply in the economy.

  3. Fuel and light
  4. Transport and communication
  5. Clothing and Education

explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer
Retail core inflation refers to the inflation rate calculated by excluding items that are highly volatile in nature. In India, retail inflation is measured using the Consumer Price Index (CPI). However, the core inflation component is a filtered version of this, which focuses on the underlying and persistent trend in prices.

Option 1 is correct. Food and beverages are excluded from core inflation because their prices are highly volatile. They are influenced by seasonal patterns, weather events, and supply shocks, which do not reflect long-term inflation trends.

Option 2 is correct. Fuel and light are also excluded as they are directly affected by international oil prices and exchange rate movements. These price changes are external and unpredictable, making them unsuitable for measuring core inflation.

Option 3 is incorrect. Transport and communication are included in core inflation. These services generally exhibit stable pricing patterns and are considered part of the structural components of CPI.

Option 4 is incorrect. Clothing and education are also part of core inflation. Their prices usually change gradually and reflect demand-supply dynamics over time, making them relevant for assessing persistent inflation.

explanation:
Solution: (a)

The circular economy is a model of production and consumption that emphasizes sharing, leasing, reusing, repairing, refurbishing, and recycling existing materials and products for as long as possible. This approach helps create a closed-loop system that minimizes waste and reduces the need for new resource extraction.
Statement I is correct: According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Sixth Assessment Report (2023), human activities such as burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and intensive agriculture have contributed significantly to global warming, leading to an estimated 1.1°C increase in average temperature since the early 20th century. A circular economy mitigates these impacts by reducing waste, lowering resource consumption, and decreasing greenhouse gas emissions through sustainable practices.
Statement II is correct: With the global population increasing, so does the demand for raw materials. However, many essential natural resources are finite. The circular economy reduces dependence on virgin materials by promoting the reuse and recycling of products, conserving resources, and protecting ecosystems, thereby supporting biodiversity.
Statement III is correct: The circular economy also targets waste reduction during production by promoting efficient design and resource reuse. For example, agricultural waste like animal manure is repurposed into organic fertilizer and biogas, which supports sustainable farming and energy use.
As circular economy helps to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions through low raw material consumption and low waste production, option a is the correct answer: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I

1. With reference to casual workers employed in India, consider the following statements:
  2. All casual workers are entitled for Employees Provident Fund Coverage.
  3. All casual workers are entitled for regular working hours and overtime payment.
  4. The government can by a notification specify that an establishment or industry shall pay wages only through its bank account.
    Which of the above statement are correct? [UPSC CSE Pre 2022]
explanation:
Solution: (b)
Exp) Option b is the correct answer.
Statement 1 is incorrect. A casual worker is a worker on a temporary employment contract with generally limited entitlements to benefits and little or no security of employment. The main attribute is the absence of a continuing relationship of any stability with an employer, which could lead to their not being considered ‘employees’ at all.
Note: Though Supreme Court had ruled that casual workers are also entitled to social security benefits under the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act. “As per Section 2(f) of the EPF Act, the definition of an employee is an inclusive definition, and is widely worded to include any person engaged either directly or indirectly in connection with the work of an establishment, and is paid wages,” a bench of SC said. But the word ‘All’ makes the statement extreme and would not be true always thus the statement is incorrect.
Statement 2 is correct. Casual workers (should) have all those rights that are enjoyed by regular workers, since the definition of employee includes casual labour as per Supreme Court guidelines. Employees in India are entitled for regular working hours and overtime payment according to Minimum Wages Rules, 1950.
Statement 3 is correct. The Payment of Wages (Amendment) Act 2017 provides that the Government may specify that the employer of any industrial or other establishment shall pay wages to every employee only by cheque or by crediting the wages in his bank account.
