  • Organizing Seed Production in Clustered Areas: The concept involves concentrating seed production in specific clusters or compact regions.The focus is on producing seeds locally within the cluster to meet the demands of the area.
  • Replacing Local Varieties with High-Yielding Varieties: The aim is to replace traditional or local crop varieties with newer, high-yielding varieties. This helps improve overall agricultural productivity and crop yield.
  • Increasing Seed Production: The goal is to enhance the quantity of seed production within the cluster. This ensures a sufficient supply of seeds for local farmers.
  • Meeting Local Demand with Timely Supply and Reasonable Cost: The emphasis is on providing seeds that are needed by local farmers at the right time and at an affordable price. This ensures that farmers have access to quality seeds without financial burden.
  • Increasing Seed Replacement Rate: The focus is on encouraging farmers to replace their existing seeds with new varieties. This leads to higher adoption of improved cultivars and better agricultural practices.

question: 1. The approximate representation of land use classification in India is-
explanation:
Exp) Option d is the correct answer.

The approximate representation of land use classification in India is as follows: Net area sown occupies around 47% of the land, forests cover about 23%, and other areas, which include non-agricultural land, constitute approximately 30% of the total land area.

Important Tips

Nine-fold Classification of Land Use in India:

  • Forests: This category encompasses all lands designated as forests by legal enactments or administered as forests, whether state-owned or private, wooded or potential forest land. It includes the area of crops and grazing lands within the forests.
  • Area under Non-agricultural Uses: This includes lands occupied by buildings, roads, railways, water bodies (rivers, canals), and areas utilized for purposes other than agriculture.
  • Barren and Unculturable Land: Encompasses lands like mountains, deserts, and areas that cannot be cultivated without excessive cost. It covers land not suitable for cultivation, either due to topography or cost constraints.
  • Permanent Pastures and Grazing Lands: This category includes grazing lands, whether permanent pastures, meadows, or village common grazing lands.
  • Land under Miscellaneous Tree Crops, etc.: It includes cultivable land used for agricultural purposes other than ‘Net Area Sown,’ such as groves for fuel, bamboo bushes, thatching grasses, and Casuarina trees.
  • Culturable Waste Land: Covers land available for cultivation but not utilized for cultivation during the current year or the last five years, either fallow or covered with shrubs and jungles.
  • Fallow Lands other than Current Fallows: Encompasses lands temporarily out of cultivation for a period of more than one year and less than five years.
  • Current Fallows: Represents cropped areas left fallow during the current year due to various reasons, including lack of cultivation.
  • Net Area Sown: The total area sown with crops and orchards, counted only once even if sown multiple times within the same year. This category indicates the actual cultivated area.

question: 1. Gandhi Sagar Dam is a part of which one of the following?
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.

The Gandhi Sagar Dam is a part of the Chambal Project, which is a multipurpose river valley project that involves the construction of four major dams on the Chambal River and its tributaries. The project aims to provide irrigation, drinking water, power generation and flood control to the states of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

Important Tips

The four dams of the Chambal Project are:

  • The Gandhi Sagar Dam, which is the first and largest dam of the project. It is located in Mandsaur district of Madhya Pradesh and has a gross storage capacity of 7.322 billion cubic metres.
  • The Rana Pratap Sagar Dam, which is the second dam of the project. It is located in Chittorgarh district of Rajasthan and has a gross storage capacity of 1.566 billion cubic metres.
  • The Jawahar Sagar Dam, which is the third dam of the project. It is located in Kota district of Rajasthan and has a gross storage capacity of 0.113 billion cubic metres.
  • The Kota Barrage, which is the fourth and final dam of the project. It is located in Kota district of Rajasthan and has a gross storage capacity of 0.047 billion cubic metres.

question:
1. Consider the following statements:
  2. Molasses is a by-product of the sugar production process.
  3. Bagasse obtained from sugar mills is used as a fuel in the boilers to generate steam in sugar factories.
  4. Sugar can only be produced from sugarcane as the raw material.
    Which of these statements is/are correct?
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer

Molasses is the thick syrup that results from the refining of sugarcane or sugar beets into sugar. It is byproduct of sugar production process. It contains a good amount of vitamin B6 and minerals like calcium, magnesium, iron, and manganese. Hence Statement 1 is correct.

Bagasse is the remnant left after extracting the juice of the sugarcane or sorghum is known as bagasse. It is a dry pulpy fibrous material. It is used for the generation of heat energy and electricity. The sugar mills use it as their primary fuel source, as it generates sufficient energy to fully power a sugar mill. Ethanol produced from it is also used as a popular fuel in some countries. Hence Statement 2 is correct.

Sugar can also be extracted from Sugar beet, Sweet Sorghum, Corn and other sources as the raw material. Hence Statement 3 is incorrect.

question:
1. Consider the following statements:
  2. India is the original home of the cotton plant
  3. India is the first country in the world to develop hybrid cotton variety leading to increased production
    Which of these statements is/are correct?
explanation:
Exp) Option c is the correct answer

India is believed to be the original home of the cotton plant. Hence statement 1 is correct.

Cotton is one of the main raw materials for cotton textile industry. India is the first country in the world to develop hybrid cotton variety leading to increased production. The first cotton hybrid H4 (Sankar-4) was released for commercial cultivation in 1970 from Cotton Research Station, Surat by Dr. C.T. Patel. After this, the area under hybrid cultivation started increasing due to its high yielding potential and wider adaptability. Hence statement 2 is correct.

Important Tips

Challenges in Indian cotton cultivation

  • Around 72 % of cotton area comes under low to medium productivity, in which 65 percent area is rainfed, mainly in the Central and Southern zones.
  • Most of the rainfed area has soil with low water holding capacity, poor fertility, shallow and with less accessibility to water resource for irrigation.
  • Cotton crop is highly prone to pests like Pink bollworm, American bollworm, Whiteflies, Jassids, Thrips and Mirid bugs.
  • Predominant cotton growing farmers are having marginal land holdings.
    What make India to adopt Hybrid Cotton in large scale
  • Our country is having diverse cotton growing environment and adaptation of hybrids are better than varieties due to
  • Broader genetic base
  • Early vigour and establishment of hybrids even under rainfed conditions resulting better productivity than varieties.
  • Hybrids are responsive to better crop management practices (Eg. Fertilizer response)
  • It is possible to Combine multiple traits like
  • Biotic & abiotic stress tolerant
  • Higher yield with better fibre quality.

1. Consider the following statements:
    Assertion (A): The Eastern coast of India produces more rice than the Western coast.
    Reason (R): The Eastern coast receives more rainfall than the Western coast.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true individually and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true individually but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation:
Exp) Option c is the correct answer.

Assertion (A) is true- The eastern coast provides ideal conditions for rice cultivation such as the conditions of temperature ranging from 20-27°C, the presence of heavy clay soil, and ample rainfall (175-300 cm). This is why, the Eastern Coast of India produces more rice than Western Coast.

Reason (R) is false- The Western Coast receives more rainfall than the Eastern Coast. The western coastal plain of India lies on the windward side of the southwest monsoon winds, which brings orographic rainfall to it. The winds rise up the Western Ghats mountains, cool, and condense, releasing their moisture as rain. The winds on descending the slopes of the mountains towards the leeward sides have no moisture or very less moisture left, hence bringing less rain to the eastern coastal plains

question: 1. Which one of the following organisms can serve as a biofertilizer for rice crops?
explanation:
Exp) Option a is the correct answer.

Blue-green algae are nitrogen-fixing organisms that can be used as biofertilizers for rice crops. They are also known as cyanobacteria. They can fix atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia, which is a form of nitrogen that plants can use. This helps to increase the nitrogen content of the soil, which can lead to increased crop yields.
